chief_complaint: chronic pain over lateral elbow worsening with wrist extension and gripping tools
hpi_details: 42M plumber presenting with point tenderness at lateral humeral epicondyle and pain reproduced by resisted wrist extension with elbow fully extended.
ideas: He thinks he pulled a tendon or pinched a nerve in his arm from constantly tightening heavy pipe fittings.
concerns: He is worried that his grip will give out permanently and leave him unable to work and earn a living as a plumber.
expectations: He hopes to get a supportive elbow brace and strong anti-inflammatory medication so he can finish his plumbing jobs this week.

teaching.one_liner: 42M plumber with chronic lateral elbow pain worsened by wrist extension and gripping tools.

must_ask.objective: Characterize the pain location and triggers
must_ask.say: Can you point exactly where it hurts, and does gripping tools make it worse?
How much repetitive gripping or wrist motion does your plumbing work require?

must_ask.objective: Assess duration and prior treatments tried
must_ask.say: How long has this been going on, and have you tried anything for it?

must_ask.objective: Screen for neck symptoms to exclude radiculopathy
must_ask.say: Do you have any neck pain or numbness going down your arm?

must_ask.objective: Explain the bracing and rehabilitation plan
must_ask.say: We recommend a counterforce brace, stretching exercises, and modifying your grip technique at work.

history.answer: The outside of my right elbow has been aching for weeks, and it gets really sharp whenever I grip tools or bend my wrist back.
It is just my right elbow, right on the bony bump on the outer side. None of my other joints hurt.
It started gradually about two months ago and has been getting steadily worse as work picked up.
Most of the time it is a dull ache, but it turns into a sharp, burning pain whenever I grasp something tightly. I would rate it about a 6 out of 10.
No, I haven't seen any swelling, redness, or heat around the elbow. It looks completely normal from the outside.
My elbow feels a little stiff when I first wake up, but it loosens up in less than five minutes once I move my arm around.
Resting my arm over the weekend helps calm it down, but the pain flares right back up as soon as I start working with my hands again.
I work as a plumber, and using pipe wrenches, screwdrivers, and carrying heavy pipes makes the pain unbearable. Turning doorknobs or lifting a heavy skillet also hurts.
I tried taking some over-the-counter ibuprofen and putting ice packs on it after work, which took the edge off for an hour or two, but the pain always returns.
No, I never had a direct fall, hit, or pop in my elbow. It just came on from all the heavy wrenching at work.
No, my neck feels fine, and I don't have any pain, tingling, or numbness shooting down my arm or into my fingers.
No, I have never had pain like this in my elbow before.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or sweats.
No, my energy is good, and I haven't had any unusual fatigue or weight loss.
No, my skin is clear, and I have no rashes, mouth sores, eye redness, or hair loss.
No, I do not have any lower back stiffness in the morning, heel pain, or swollen fingers.
No, I haven't had any diarrhea, stomach bugs, painful urination, or recent sore throats.
I drink a beer or two on the weekend, but I do not drink heavily, and I don't eat unusual amounts of red meat or take water pills.
No, I have never had any joint injections, surgery on my arms, or taken steroids.
I have been married for fifteen years and have only been intimate with my wife, with no new partners.
I figured I probably pulled a tendon or pinched a nerve from wrenching heavy pipes all day.
I'm worried that my grip will get so weak that I won't be able to handle my tools and earn a living.
I was hoping to get an elbow brace and some strong anti-inflammatories so I can keep working this week.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or arthritis.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I do not take any prescription medications or daily supplements, just the occasional ibuprofen when my elbow flares up.
I have no known allergies to any medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I work full-time as an independent plumbing contractor and live in a house with my wife and two kids.
My parents are both healthy in their seventies, and there is no family history of rheumatoid arthritis, gout, or autoimmune diseases.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, temperature 36.7 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Marked focal tenderness over the right lateral humeral epicondyle without joint effusion, warmth, or redness; full active and passive elbow range of motion.
Resisted right wrist extension with the elbow fully extended reproduces sharp pain at the lateral epicondyle; full 5/5 motor strength throughout bilateral upper extremities.
Intact sensation to light touch and pinprick across bilateral upper extremities, including radial, median, and ulnar nerve distributions.
Biceps, brachioradialis, and triceps deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally.
Full cervical spine range of motion without midline tenderness; Spurling test is negative bilaterally with no radiating arm symptoms.
No rash, psoriatic plaques, subcutaneous nodules, or tophi over the elbows, hands, or extensor surfaces.
